requests.text: Next: revise `uniqueBy` to track seen values with a type-preserving identity store, e.g. a `Map` keyed by the raw `item[key]` value, checking existence with `seen.has(k)` instead of object-property truthiness. This directly targets E3 failures `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key` on `unique.mjs@12e22056`, while preserving the already-passing order, first-value, empty-input, and immutability behavior. Re-run the fixture on the same artifact: full passes would falsify the object-property-coercion explanation, and any remaining failure should be narrowed as a separate issue.

Next step for E3: in `unique.mjs`, switch the seen store from a plain object to a `Map` and test membership with `has(k)` before `set(k, true)`. That directly targets `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key`, since a `Map` preserves numeric-vs-string keys and has no prototype-name collisions; keep the existing filter to preserve first values and input order without mutation. Falsifiable check: after that single-file rewrite, those three checks should pass while `empty-input`, `first-value-kept`, `missing-key-once`, `original-order`, and `immutable-input` remain passing.

Next step: revise `uniqueBy` to track seen keys in a `Map` keyed directly by `item[key]` (`seen.has(k)` before `seen.set(k, true)`), preserving the existing filter/first-order/no-mutation shape. This targets E3’s failed `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key` checks: `Map` distinguishes `1` from `'1'` and safely handles keys like `'toString'`/`'__proto__'`, whereas the current plain-object truthiness check conflates them. Minimal distinguishing observation: re-run those three checks and expect the typed-key/prototype-key/custom-key arrays to be retained correctly.

Next: in `uniqueBy`, replace the plain `seen` object with a `Set` (or `Map`) and check raw key identity with `has`: `const k = item[key]; if (seen.has(k)) return false; seen.add(k); return true;`, keeping the existing `filter`, first-value, order, and no-mutation shape. This targets E3 failures `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key` on `unique.mjs@12e22056...`; after the single-file rewrite those should pass while `empty-input`, `first-value-kept`, `missing-key-once`, `original-order`, and `immutable-input` remain passing. Any remaining E3 failure should then be narrowed as a separate issue.

Next: rewrite `uniqueBy` to track raw `item[key]` identity with a `Set`/`Map` membership check (`seen.has(k)` before adding), preserving the existing `filter`, first-value, input-order, empty-input, and no-mutation behavior. This directly targets E3 failures `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key` on `unique.mjs@12e22056d8ea59bbd956668f5b9f3587ff504d7568dc151b381ec04f56613c5d`. Falsifiable check: after that single-file edit, those three checks should pass while `empty-input`, `first-value-kept`, `missing-key-once`, `original-order`, and `immutable-input` remain passing. If any still fails, record the raw `k`, its type, and the `seen.has(k)` outcome as the minimal distinguishing observation.
